cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The handbook says lock the hall at six. Our festival permit says stay open till eight. Which governs tonight? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the front open and lock the back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. So the permit governs public access, and the handbook governs everything else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Including the kitchen closing at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are we canceling the seven-o'clock supper, or does the permit govern kitchens too?

mechanism: A coordinates hall closing and adopts B door compromise while requiring a choice of governing rule when supper exposes its boundary.
confusable: Unlike simply choosing a convenient action, A keeps asking which existing authority governs the specific action.
comparison: Handbook versus festival permit differs from competing seating and birthday traditions.
seedUse: D178-a six/eight rules, split doors and seven supper; S02-a takes locking work under B interpretation.
